tables.how: Of the 32 local committees with a union in their name that took in $100,000 or more since 2015, 9 took half or more from outside unions and their members. This is every Schedule A receipt of those 9: $8,026,226 raised, $6,988,244 of it from outside. A giver is a union or labor committee when its name reads as one; an individual giving under $1,000 is counted with members and small donors; every other giver counts as outside labor. The other 23 committees, funded mostly by unions and their members (31,484 receipts, $13,810,814), are not listed here; their receipts from City payees are in the next list.
tables.limits: All of this is disclosed. A committee that spends on its own may take unlimited amounts, and the rule against contributions from a City contractor does not reach it. Coalition committees are common, and two of these name the business sponsor in their own title. A union is recognized by its name, so a labor body with a neutral name is counted as outside. The City payee is matched by name; no row shows that a giver had a contract awaiting anyone’s approval when it gave.

tables.how: Every entry by the nine committees on Form 460 Schedule D, Form 496 or Form 465 that names a candidate or measure (244 of the 2,707 such entries by all union-named committees). The case’s spending figures are the sum of these entries across all the forms.
tables.limits: The same spending is usually reported twice: first on a 24-hour report (Form 496) and later on the committee’s regular statement (Form 460, Schedule D). Adding the forms together, as the case’s figures do, can therefore count one payment twice, which is why a committee can appear to have spent more than it raised. The column of forms lets a reader take one form at a time. Independent spending is not under the candidate’s control.
